title: Two names, two jobs
idea: MEET: a plan can have several named sub-plans, each doing its own job. No code.

exercises.prompt: A plan defines 'greet' (shows 'Hello') and 'farewell' (shows 'Bye'). These are...
exercises.explanation: Two names, two different jobs. A plan can define as many named sub-plans as it needs.

exercises.prompt: Plan: use greet, then use farewell. What appears?
exercises.explanation: greet runs first (Hello), then farewell (Bye). Each named job does its own thing, in use order.

exercises.prompt: A quiz plan might define which named jobs? (Pick all sensible ones.)
exercises.explanation: A quiz could reasonably have ask_questions, show_score, and a print_border. Painting a fence is unrelated.

exercises.prompt: Order the uses so a scoreboard shows a border, then the score, then a border.
exercises.explanation: Border, score, border - one border job used twice, the score job once. Each job has its own name.

exercises.prompt: Different jobs should get different names so you can tell them apart.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Distinct jobs need distinct, descriptive names. Two jobs sharing one name would be confusing.

exercises.prompt: Match each named job to what it shows.
exercises.explanation: Each name is tied to one clear job. The name tells you what using it will do.

exercises.prompt: You use greet twice and farewell once. How many messages appear in total?
exercises.explanation: greet runs twice (two Hellos) and farewell once (one Bye): three messages. Count each use.

exercises.prompt: Why split a plan into several named jobs instead of one big unnamed block?
options: Each job is clear, reusable, and easy to fix on its own
exercises.explanation: Several clear named jobs beat one tangle: each is readable, reusable, and independently fixable.

exercises.prompt: A single plan can define many named jobs and use each a different number of times.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Define as many as you need, and use each as often as the plan requires - even zero times.

options: a plan can hold several named jobs, each with its own name and purpose
exercises.explanation: Many named jobs, each clear and reusable. Soon you'll write several real functions in one program.
